issues.description: The problem statement specifies `simulate_msd_two_rounds(n_shots:int, p: float, batch_size:float = 1000000.0)`, but the template and solution define `batch_size` as an `int` (and use it as such for `range` batching). This type mismatch can confuse students and would break typical batching loops if followed literally from the statement.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the problem statement signature to use an integer batch size, e.g. `simulate_msd_two_rounds(n_shots: int, p: float, batch_size: int = 1000000) -> tuple[float, float]`.

issues.description: In the template, `inject` is defined as `def inject(circ: stim.Circuit, data_qubit: int, injection_qubit) -> int` (missing the `int` type annotation for `injection_qubit`), while the problem statement and solution specify `injection_qubit: int`. This inconsistency can confuse students about the intended type and weakens type-hint guidance compared to other functions.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template signature to `def inject(circ: stim.Circuit, data_qubit: int, injection_qubit: int) -> int:`.

issues.description: The template docstring for `build_msd_circ` says the second returned list contains "final X-basis measurements of the distilled state", but the problem statement requires the second list to be the measurement indices of the destructive X-basis measurements of the 15 tetrahedral-code qubits (in qubit order). This wording mismatch can cause students to return the wrong measurement indices/order.
issues.suggestedFix: Edit the `build_msd_circ` docstring in the template so the second list is described as the measurement indices for the destructive X-basis measurements of the 15 tetrahedral-code qubits (in qubit order), not measurements of `distilled_state`.
